## Supplied setup


```{r}
set.seed(6313)
markers <- data.frame(
  marker_a = round(rnorm(30, 5, 1), 2),
  marker_b = round(rnorm(30, 12, 2), 2),
  marker_c = round(rnorm(30, 8, 1.5), 2)
)
# A separate numeric matrix: rows are participants, columns are repeated visits.
visits <- matrix(round(rnorm(90, 125, 10), 1), nrow = 30, ncol = 3)
colnames(visits) <- c("baseline", "week6", "week12")
```

## 4. Run one benchmark

Run the supplied timing code. It compares a row loop, `apply()`, and `rowMeans()` after checking agreement and warming up. Report the input dimensions and which method has the smallest median time in your run. Explain why a displayed zero does not mean an operation takes no time. Recommend a method in one sentence.


```{r}
row_loop <- function(x) {
  out <- numeric(nrow(x))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(x))) out[i] <- mean(x[i, ])
  return(out)
}
row_apply <- function(x) apply(x, 1, mean)
benchmark_input <- matrix(rep(as.vector(visits), 1000), ncol = 3)
methods <- list(loop = row_loop, apply = row_apply, vectorized = rowMeans)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(row_loop(benchmark_input), rowMeans(benchmark_input))),
          isTRUE(all.equal(row_apply(benchmark_input), rowMeans(benchmark_input))))
for (fun in methods) invisible(fun(benchmark_input))
timings <- matrix(NA_real_, 5, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, names(methods)))
for (k in seq_len(nrow(timings))) {
  for (j in seq_along(methods)) {
    timings[k, j] <- system.time(methods[[j]](benchmark_input))[["elapsed"]]
  }
}
timings
apply(timings, 2, median)
dim(benchmark_input)
R.version.string
```
